title: Tech Note: Installing & Configuring Mac & PC Remote Access to a Windows NT-based 4D Server
author: David Hartje

historical_commentary.text: This note documents a specific 1996 dial-up remote-access solution (Windows NT RAS plus modems, with Windows 95 Dial-Up Networking or Mac FreePPP as clients) for reaching a Windows NT-based 4D Server remotely. Dial-up RAS/PPP-over-modem networking for LAN access is entirely obsolete, replaced first by VPNs and later by cloud/internet-native connectivity; the note is now of historical interest only, though the underlying goal of secure remote database access remains relevant, solved very differently today.
related_updates: Dial-up modem-based Remote Access Service (RAS) has been obsolete for decades, replaced first by broadband VPN connections and now largely by cloud/internet-native application access
Windows NT 3.51 and the freeware utilities referenced (FreePPP, Windows 95 Dial-Up Adapter) are all long discontinued
4D Server remote/cloud access today is typically achieved via direct TCP/IP over the internet, VPN, or ORDA-based REST access rather than dial-up RAS
